summary: Advanced the raw-evidence provenance frontier, but deliberately did not promote a locally generated bootstrap-v3 certificate after identifying that a transcript synthesized from the same pure-function structural proof would be circular evidence. Persisted the independent structural-attestation artifact and a fresh-process capture harness whose statistical unit is one protected-statistic observation in one process that exits after one job. A sequential 2,120-process capture attempt hit the 120-second tool timeout before emitting a complete transcript, so no raw challenge transcript or replay authorization was promoted this run.

new_measurement_validity_finding.name: proof-derived-challenge-data-is-circular-attestation
new_measurement_validity_finding.finding: A challenge transcript generated offline from the exact deterministic function asserted by the structural proof can make the issuance gate and certificate record internally reproducible, but it does not independently demonstrate that two fresh runtime processes produced the same protected statistic. Such a transcript therefore does not close the privileged-author/fabricated-certificate gap identified by the prior checkpoint.
new_measurement_validity_finding.consequence: Bootstrap-v3 must consume raw observations captured from actual fresh process executions, not values regenerated from the structural proof or from the certificate record. Locally generated synthetic certificate/manifest/bootstrap drafts from this run were intentionally not persisted or promoted.
new_measurement_validity_finding.negative_control: A local helper draft did reject a fabricated certificate record when raw inputs were held fixed, but that result is insufficient because the draft raw inputs themselves were proof-derived rather than independently captured.
